## Summary

The pitch: "ever tried bromantane? modafinil? semax? cerebrolysin? tadalafil? where'd you get it, and how'd it go? … ever wanted to know what other people actually thought of a compound or vendor — not an ad, not a sponsored review, just real data?" That's the new **community rating system** on basedbiohacker.com: log your experience on any compound page, watch the community average build over time, and "use it when you're deciding what to try or where to buy next."

The photo shows the score card on the bromantane page: overall rating 1–10 (poor→excellent), did-you-notice-benefit / side-effects / would-use-again toggles, a source picker (self-reported source breakdown already names **Kimera Chems** and **Real Peptides**), location field, Cloudflare Turnstile bot check, one response per account, "scores show after 5 ratings" — bromantane sat at **4 responses** at capture.

Site verified live (SPA, curl): "Evidence-aware compound research, peptide guides, practical stacks, and sourcing tools." The linked bromantane profile carries a real mechanistic writeup — Soviet-1980s actoprotector, upregulates tyrosine hydroxylase (rate-limiting enzyme for dopamine synthesis), weak dopamine reuptake inhibition, "calm, smooth energy without the stimulant edge."

## Why it matters

- **The real idea worth keeping:** crowdsourced compound→vendor→outcome data is genuinely scarce. Reddit anecdotes rot and nothing aggregates them. If this reaches critical mass it becomes a real check on the gray-market peptide/chem vendor space — Kimera Chems and Real Peptides are exactly the vendor class the vault thread already watches.
- **Cold-start reality:** the flagship example had 4 ratings with scores hidden until 5. The dataset is empty today; value depends entirely on adoption. A tweet with 78 likes does not seed n=1000.
- **Conflict-of-interest gate:** the author came into the vault through affiliate-flavored product tweets ([[2026-11-17-basedbiohacker-modvigil-200]]), and the site itself sells "sourcing tools" — the rating system grades the very vendors the site steers toward. "Not an ad, not a sponsored review" is the claim; the incentive to seed positive vendor ratings is structural. Treat averages as weak signal until provenance is visible.
- **Privacy gate:** contributing requires an account, stores answers "with your account ID," and asks location — pseudonymous health-adjacent data on a gray-market-adjacent site. Browsing is fine; contributing adds exposure for no user need (UAE posture unchanged).
- Cross-checks: bromantane context sits in the Zygomatic thread ([[2026-11-10-zygomatic03-pinealon-social-fluidity]]); modafinil in [[2026-11-10-limitlesstack-modafinil-thesis]]; yesterday's mexidol swap pitch from this same author ([[2026-11-19-basedbiohacker-mexidol-social-lubricant]]) is exactly the kind of claim this rating system would let the crowd test.
